title: FontLab Blog
description: News, technical writing, and updates from FontLab.

items.title: Five centuries of line — Dürer, Hogarth, Bewick, Doré
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

A line can carry tone, texture, shadow, and emotion — and never once pretend to be a photograph. That is the whole argument of five centuries of printmaking, made with a burin, a graver, and eventually a stylus.

items.title: Calfonts: italics that aren’t just slanted romans
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Italics are the part of a font family that most often gets shipped wrong — slanted romans, no cursive structure, lopsided ovals. The Calfonts italic tutorial walks through what it actually takes to draw an italic that earns its place next to the roman.

items.title: Briem: how to draw an italic (and why the slanted-roman trap is real)
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Italic is not roman tilted to the right. Slant your upright a and what you get is a tilted a, not an italic a — the structure is wrong, the rhythm is wrong, the connection points are wrong.

items.title: Color fonts: the next big thing? A FontLab tutorial
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Back in 2014, color fonts were a brand new frontier. This 103-minute tutorial with Adam Twardoch was one of the first deep dives into how to actually make them.

items.title: Basics of Python scripting in FontLab Studio 5
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Automation unlocks the real power of a professional font editor. In this 70-minute tutorial, Adam Twardoch introduces Python scripting inside FontLab Studio 5.

items.title: How to space a font
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Spacing is where type design lives or dies. In this 53-minute tutorial, Thomas Phinney walks through sidebearings, optical principles, and the practical workflow inside FontLab Studio 5.

items.title: FontLab VI 6.1: components, sidebar filters, and metrics expressions
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab VI 6.1 arrived in October 2018. It added standards-compliant components, a Font window sidebar for glyph filtering, and linked metrics expressions.

items.title: Introducing FontLab 7: the pro font editor, evolved
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab 7 is a major upgrade to FontLab VI, arriving after a summer and autumn of concentrated work, with more than 250 new features, fixes, and improvements.

items.title: Bézier and de Casteljau: two engineers, one beautiful curve
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

In 1958, Paul de Casteljau at Citroën worked out the mathematics of the curves we now draw with every day. A few years later Pierre Bézier at Renault arrived at the same idea independently and published it in 1962.

items.title: FontLab Studio 5 and the Fontographer acquisition
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

2005 was a pivotal year for Fontlab Ltd. The company shipped FontLab Studio 5, which became the dominant professional font editor for the next decade. FontLab also acquired Fontographer from Macromedia, reviving a tool that had been dormant since the mid-1990s.

items.title: TransType 4 for Mac and Windows
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

TransType 4 arrived in December 2013 as a complete rewrite of our font conversion app. It added multi-color OpenType output and web font export to its core toolkit.

items.title: FontLab Studio 5.2.1 for Windows
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab Studio 5.2.1 for Windows shipped in December 2013. It builds on the 5.2 foundation with new tools and hundreds of bug fixes.

items.title: Matthew Carter webinar
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

In February 2014, FontLab hosted a live webinar with Matthew Carter, a key figure in digital type design.

items.title: Brush Romans webinar with John Downer and Paul Herrera
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

On March 11, 2014, FontLab hosted a webinar on Roman capital letterforms and their origins in flat-brush writing. Sign painter and type designer John Downer presented alongside calligrapher Paul Herrera.

items.title: DTL OTMaster 5.0, vfb2ufo, and FontLab Pad 1.1
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

December 2014 brought a major update to DTL OTMaster, plus two new free tools. We released a command-line UFO converter and an updated color font typesetter.

items.title: FontLab VI is here
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab Studio 5 was a workhorse. It shipped in 2004 and carried a generation of type designers through the OpenType transition. The app aged gracefully, right up until it didn’t. On 7 December 2017, we replaced it.

items.title: DTL OTMaster 7.9 available now
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb}

DTL OTMaster 7.9 adds support for variable OpenType fonts. This includes the fvar, gvar, CFF2, STAT, HVAR, and MVAR tables. It includes a new Proofing Tool for printing and exporting PDF specimens, and a Side-by-Side Viewer that shows variation instances.

Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux. A full license is US$228. Upgrades from previous versions are US$57.

items.title: FontLab VI: 12 releases in 12 months
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab VI 6.1.2 shipped today. That made twelve updates in twelve months after the first public version of our new font editor.

items.title: Design space axes and multiple masters in FontLab VI
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Variable fonts force you to think in multiple dimensions at once. This four-minute video shows exactly how to set up a design space with axes and masters in FontLab VI. It gives you a concise, visual introduction to the core concepts behind variable font production.

items.title: From sketch to font in minutes with built-in ScanFont
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

This two-minute demo of the built-in ScanFont feature has over 40,000 views. It earns that attention by showing something genuinely useful in record time. You scan or photograph hand-drawn letterforms, paste them into FontLab, and the software traces them into editable outlines.

items.title: FontLab Studio 5, Fontographer 5 and TypeTool 3 on macOS 10.15 Catalina
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

macOS 10.15 Catalina drops all 32-bit app support, which means FontLab Studio 5, Fontographer 5, TypeTool 3, and BitFonter 3 for Mac will not run on it — and porting them to 64-bit is not feasible. If you are on Catalina, your options are CrossOver Mac 19 (run the Windows versions via a thin emulation layer), a virtual machine running an older macOS or Windows, or upgrading to the 64-bit FontLab 7.

items.title: FontLab 7.1: ink traps, harmonized handles, and quick measurement
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab 7.1 landed in March 2020 as a free update to all FontLab 7 users, delivering over 70 new and improved features and 80 fixes across five point releases between March and August 2020. The headline additions — ink traps, harmonized handles, looped corners, and quick measurement — gave designers finer control over node behavior and optical geometry than any prior version.

items.title: Say hello to FontLab 7.2
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab 7.2 is a free update with 120 new or improved features. The headline: interpolation now runs 30× faster. New tools include Rotate, Scale, and Slant; an adaptive freeform grid with Suggest Distance; variable and attached components; visual OpenType feature proofing; and Microsoft VOLT integration. Existing FontLab 7 users get it free; FontLab VI users can upgrade for $99.

items.title: Import artwork into FontLab 7
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Most type designers don’t draw directly in the font editor — they sketch in pencil, refine in Illustrator or Affinity Designer, then need to get that artwork into FontLab cleanly. This eight-minute video from Dave Lawrence’s FontLab 7 series shows exactly how.

items.title: Basics of spacing in FontLab 7
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Spacing is the invisible work that determines whether a font feels effortless or labored to read. This five-minute tutorial from Dave Lawrence’s FontLab 7 series strips the topic down to its essentials: what sidebearings are, how to set them in the metrics window, and how to evaluate spacing visually as you work.

items.title: FontLab 7: a year in updates
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab 7 launched in December 2019 with over 250 new features. Twelve months later, it has rather more than that. Here is what the 2020 update cycle actually delivered — not counting FontLab 7.2, which has its own post.

items.title: Make your variable fonts better with FontLab 7
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

This 19-minute presentation by Adam Twardoch, delivered at ATypI Tech Talks 2021, goes beyond building variable fonts to the harder question: making them good. It covers quality assurance, interpolation checking, and the tools in FontLab 7 and related applications that help catch problems before a variable font ships.

items.title: Rescue your PostScript Type 1 fonts
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

PostScript Type 1 fonts are on their way out. Adobe is ending Type 1 support in Creative Cloud applications in early 2023, and Apple has signalled the same direction in macOS. If you have a library of Type 1 fonts — and many working designers do — now is the time to convert them to OpenType.

items.title: FontLab 7.2.0.7644 and macOS 12.3 Monterey
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

Apple’s macOS 12.3 Monterey update broke all previous versions of FontLab 7 by removing the system Python 2.7 that FontLab depended on. FontLab 7.2.0.7644 is a free patch that restores compatibility — macOS 12.3 users need to install a bundled Python 2.7 package alongside the app. A buggy intermediate build (7650) that made glyph fills transparent was withdrawn; 7644 does not have that problem.

items.title: Hello, FontLab 8
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Two years into FontLab 7, users had a clear message: the drawing engine is excellent, the variable font support is solid, now make the rest of the application match. FontLab 8, shipping today, is our answer.
